'''Dmitrii "Dima" F. Perepichka''' (born 1972) is the Chair of Chemistry Department<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mcgill.ca/chemistry/faculty/dima-perepichka|title=Dima Perepichka|website=Department of Chemistry|accessdate=20 August 2018}}</ref> and Sir William C. MacDonald Chair [[Professor]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mcgill.ca/chemistry/channels/news/dima-perepichka-becomes-sir-william-c-macdonald-chair-chemistry-266555|title=Dima Perepichka becomes Sir William C. Macdonald Chair in Chemistry|website=Department of Chemistry|accessdate=20 August 2018}}</ref> in [[Chemistry]] at [[McGill University]]. His research interest are primarily in the area of [[organic electronics]]. He has contributed in the understanding of structural electronics effects of organic conjugated materials at molecular, supramolecular, and macromolecular levels via the study of small molecules, supramolecular (co-)assemblies, polymers, [[covalent organic frameworks]], and on-surface assemblies/polymers.

== Research and publications ==
Prof. Perepichka has authored more than 200 publications on a diverse range of topics such as [[Conjugated system]], [[Organic semiconductor]], [[Covalent organic framework]], [[Phosphor|Organic room-temperature phosphors]], [[Organic solar cell]], [[Organic radical|Organic persistent radicals]], etc. in top-tier chemistry and materials journals such as Nature Materials<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Galeotti|first1=G.|last2=De Marchi|first2=F.|last3=Hamzehpoor|first3=E.|display-authors=etal|title=Synthesis of mesoscale ordered two-dimensional π-conjugated polymers with semiconducting properties|journal=Nature Materials|date=2020|volume=19|issue=8 |pages=874–880|doi=10.1038/s41563-020-0682-z|pmid=32424372 |bibcode=2020NatMa..19..874G |s2cid=218682687 |arxiv=2307.03433}}</ref> Nature Chemistry,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hamzehpoor|first1=E|last2=Ruchlin|first2=C.|display-authors=etal|title=Efficient room-temperature phosphorescence of covalent organic frameworks through covalent halogen doping|journal=Nature Chemistry|date=2022|volume=15|issue=1|pages=83–90|doi=10.1038/s41557-022-01070-4|pmid=36302870|s2cid=253183290}}</ref> Journal of the American Chemical Society,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Hamzehpoor|first1=E.|display-authors=etal|title=Synthesis of Boroxine and Dioxaborole Covalent Organic Frameworks via Transesterification and Metathesis of Pinacol Boronates|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|date=2021|volume=143|issue=33 |pages=13274–13280|doi=10.1021/jacs.1c05987|pmid=34428908 }}</ref> Angewandte Chemie International Edition,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Liu|first1=C.-H.|display-authors=etal|title=A Pure‐Red Doublet Emission with 90% Quantum Yield: Stable, Colorless, Iodinated Triphenylmethane Solid|journal=Angew. Chem. Int. Ed.|date=2020|volume=59|issue=51 |pages=23030–23034|doi=10.1002/anie.202009867 |pmid=32822514 |s2cid=225132059 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Che|first1=Y.|display-authors=etal|title=Mechanism of the Photodegradation of A‐D‐A Acceptors for Organic Photovoltaics|journal=Angew. Chem. Int. Ed.|date=2021|volume= 60|issue=47 |pages=24833–24837|doi=10.1002/anie.202109357 |pmid=34506067 }}</ref> etc. to name a few.
